title.narrative: Taskforce on Nature-related Financial Disclosures programme

description.narrative: Defra is one of the largest funders of the global, market-led, and science-based Taskforce on Nature-related Financial Disclosures (TNFD) initiative. The TNFD recommendations and supporting implementation guidance enable organisations to assess, report, and act on their evolving nature-related risks, opportunities, impacts, and dependencies, with the ultimate aim of supporting a shift in global financial flows towards nature-positive outcomes and achieving the goals of the Global Biodiversity Framework. Defra contributed £2,626,855 to support the TNFD initiative’s two-year open innovation ‘design and development’ phase, which culminated in the launch of the final TNFD corporate reporting recommendations on nature-related risk management and disclosure in September 2023 at New York Climate Week. From November 2021 – November 2022, Defra also contributed £1,675,000 to fund a TNFD African Voice pilot programme, with Financial Sector Deepening Africa (FSD Africa) acting as the delivery partner. This funding was used to secure engagement by African financial institutions, governments, and central banks, with the aim of ensuring that the TNFD framework is fit for purpose in African contexts. In addition, this funding supported the production of a report examining the materiality of nature-related risks for financial institutions in African contexts. At COP28 in December 2023, the Defra Secretary of State announced an additional £2 million funding to support the TNFD initiative’s global market uptake phase, which is focused on encouraging and enabling voluntary market adoption across sectors and geographies, and supporting efforts to address the knowledge, capacity building and data needs of market participants. In March 2025, Defra approved an additional £1 million funding support for the work of the TNFD's global market uptake phase.

title.narrative: TNFD Business Case Change Control Note 2025 - 2026

description.narrative: The TNFD Business Case Change Control Note 2025 – 2026 sets out how the UK Government will provide £1 million additional funding to support the TNFD’s ongoing global market uptake phase. The Change Control Note includes the relevant strategic, commercial, economic, financial, and management cases pertaining to the proposed funding. It sets out the rationale for the funding, outlines the expected results and impacts, and explains how the programme ensures value for money.

The Log-frame (or Logical Framework) is a target-setting and monitoring tool, which is used to assess the progress and effectiveness of the programme. The Log-frame tracks progress against key performance indicators – considering expected milestones, outputs and outcomes.

title.narrative: TNFD African Voice Business Case Addendum 2021-2022

description.narrative: The Addendum sets out how the UK Government will provide ~£1.6 million to support a ‘TNFD African Voice’ pilot programme, with FSD Africa (a specialist development agency set up by FCDO) acting as the delivery partner. The Addendum sets out the objectives of the funding, the expected results, in addition to the strategic, commercial, economic, financial and management cases. The goal of this pilot programme is to secure engagement by African financial institutions, governments, and central banks, with the aim of ensuring that the TNFD framework is fit for purpose in African contexts. It will also support the production of a report examining the materiality of nature-related risks for financial institutions in African contexts

The Original TNFD Business Case sets out how the funding support provided through the programme will deliver impact and contribute to Defra’s strategic and policy objectives. It sets out the financial, governance, management and risk arrangements in place, in addition to explaining how commercial procurement will be planned and managed. It specifies the monitoring, evaluation, and learning processes in place, explains how the programme ensures value for money, and designates roles and responsibilities. The Original Business Case for ~£2.8 million sets out how the UK Government will provide a financial contribution to support the TNFD’s two-year open innovation ‘design and development’ phase over 2021-2023.

title.narrative: TNFD Business Case Change Control Note 2023-2025

description.narrative: The TNFD Business Case Change Control Note 2023-2025 sets out how the UK Government will provide £2 million funding to support the TNFD’s global uptake phase. This follows the successful completion of the TNFD’s ‘design and development’ phase which culminated in the launch of the final TNFD recommendations on nature-related risk management and disclosure and supporting implementation guidance in September 2023. The TNFD’s global uptake phase is focused on encouraging and enabling voluntary market adoption across sectors and geographies, working with standards bodies, and supporting efforts to address the knowledge, capacity building, and data needs of market participants. The Change Control Note includes the relevant strategic, commercial, economic, financial, and management cases pertaining to the proposed funding. It sets out the rationale for the funding, outlines the expected results and impacts, and explains how the programme ensures value for money.

The 2022 Annual Review was conducted one year after the initiation of the TNFD programme, while the TNFD initiative was half-way through in its ‘design and development’ phase. The Annual Review process provides an opportunity to assess progress against agreed targets and milestones. It supports risk management and decision-making processes, including by reflecting on lessons learned and formulating recommendations for the year ahead.

The 2025 Annual Review assesses the TNFD’s performance in delivering the ambitions of its global market uptake phase. The Annual Review process provides an opportunity to assess progress against agreed targets and milestones. It supports risk management and decision-making processes, including by reflecting on lessons learned and formulating recommendations for the year ahead.

The Programme Completion Review was completed in 2023, following the launch of the final TNFD recommendations (which marked the end of the TNFD’s ‘design and development phase’). The Programme Completion Review assessed progress against agreed targets and milestones. It supported risk management and decision-making processes, including by reflecting on lessons learned and formulating recommendations for future programming.

The Log-frame (or Logical Framework) is a target-setting and monitoring tool, which is used to assess the progress and effectiveness of the programme. The Log-frame tracks progress against key performance indicators – considering expected milestones, outputs and outcomes.
